transcript: Lewis, Pete Bevan. Have you got any work at the Food Hall — shelf-stacking, deliveries, garden bits out the back? I need something regular.

Pete. Work's thin, I won't dress it up. I've got Owen on the shop floor and takings barely cover wages some weeks. What I could use is someone for deliveries and the bits out the back — a few hours, not full-time money. What sort of regular are you after, and what can you do?

A few hours is a start, but I'll be straight with you — I need it to add up. What's the rate, and how many hours a week are we talking? If it's steady, even part-time, I'll take it and keep looking for the rest. I can do deliveries, lifting, and I'm handy in a garden — the back of the Food Hall could do with a tidy-up, I'd wager.

Straight answer then: I can give you eight hours a week, deliveries and the back yard, at twelve dollars an hour — that's ninety-six a week, paid on the Friday like the rest of us. It's not full-time money and I won't pretend it is. If that works for you, start Wednesday morning and we'll see how the takings hold up.
[Lewis Pryce: Your job offer (r3) went to Pete Bevan.]

Eight hours at twelve — ninety-six a week. That's not enough on its own, but it's steady and I'll take it. Wednesday morning, I'll be there. One thing: if the takings pick up and there's more hours going, I want first shout at them.
[Pete Bevan: You accepted Lewis's request. You now work at Quarry Road Food Hall for $96 a week, starting now.]
Good. Wednesday, seven sharp — bring boots for the yard. And you've got first shout on extra hours if trade picks up; I'll not forget it. Anything else before you go?
